q: Girona won the first leg of their 2015 play-off semi-final 3-0 away at Zaragoza. What happened next?
a: They lost 4-1 at home and went out on away goals
sub: Four days earlier a stoppage-time Lugo equaliser had cost them automatic promotion.
note: Zaragoza 0-3 Girona, Girona 1-4 Zaragoza, out on away goals: en.wikipedia 2015 play-offs. Sub fixed: the 1-1 v Lugo was 7 June, four days before the first leg (LaLiga.com, ESPN).

q: On 20 December 2014, Numancia and Lugo played the highest-scoring game of that Segunda season. What was the score?
note: Numancia 6-6 Lugo, 20 Dec 2014, the season's highest-scoring game: en.wikipedia 2014-15 Segunda; es.wikipedia results grid.

q: When Atlético Madrid went down in 2000, their reserve side were relegated too without finishing in the drop zone. Why?
a: A reserve side cannot play in the same division as its first team
sub: Atlético B had been second in the Segunda the year before.
note: Atlético B 17th in 1999-2000 but dragged down; 2nd in 1998-99: es.wikipedia Atlético Madrileño; en.wikipedia 1999-2000 Segunda lists them relegated.

q: Which future mayor of New York bought a share in Real Oviedo during the 2012 rescue campaign?
sub: He tweeted about it in November 2012.
note: Real. Mamdani tweeted in Nov 2012 that he had bought a share during the #SOSRealOviedo drive; Carlos Slim separately took the controlling stake. Confirmed by Maldita.es, Forbes Spain, AOL and en.wikipedia Real Oviedo.

q: When SD Compostela were wound up in 2006, their property was sold off. What did a former president pay about 61,000 euros for?
sub: The buyer was José Albarrán.
note: Liquidation auctions confirmed, but the claim that the league place was sold rests only on en.wikipedia. Rewritten to the doubly sourced fact: ex-president José Albarrán paid about 61,000 euros for the trophies (es.wikipedia citing Galicia Hoxe, 4 July 2006; en.wikipedia mentions the trophies were auctioned).

q: In January 2009 a club with nine seasons of La Liga behind it took the field with only nine players, in protest at unpaid wages. Which club?
sub: They did not turn up for the next game and were withdrawn from the competition.
note: Nine players v Arnedo, 4 Jan 2009, then no-show and withdrawn; nine La Liga seasons: en and es.wikipedia CD Logroñés.

q: Rayo fans protesting the owners in 2011 tore what off their own stadium?
a: The letters spelling Teresa Rivero, the name the stadium then carried
note: Fans tore off the Teresa Rivero letters during the 2011 protests: es.wikipedia Rayo Vallecano.

q: Xerez players protested about unpaid wages in the 2000s in an unusual way. What did they do?
note: Only source is an uncited line in en and es.wikipedia Xerez; no press report found in Spanish or English searches. Cannot confirm.

q: Why do Xerez spell their name with an X when their city is Jerez?
a: It is the old spelling of the city, used after the Reconquista
sub: The pronunciation is the same.
note: Xerez is the post-Reconquista spelling, same sound: en and es.wikipedia Xerez CD. Moved to hard, a guessable answer that does not make a table gasp.

q: UD Salamanca were liquidated in June 2013. What anniversary did that fall on?
a: Their 90th, the club was founded in 1923
note: Liquidated 18 June 2013, 90 years after its 1923 foundation: en.wikipedia UD Salamanca. Moved to extreme, not a BALL answer.

q: Real Murcia were relegated from the Segunda by LaLiga in 2014, not on the pitch. Which club kept their Segunda place as a result?
sub: Murcia had finished fourth and reached the play-offs.
note: The AFE strike threat appears only in es.wikipedia, not found in press searches. Rewritten to the confirmed fact: Mirandés took the place (periodicodeibiza 2014, LaLiga statements, es.wikipedia). Moved to extreme.

q: Reus's players were offered their wages by LaLiga in late 2018 but turned it down. Why?
a: It did not cover the coaching staff and other workers, and meant relegation anyway
note: LaLiga offered to pay players but not staff, and it meant administrative relegation: es.wikipedia CF Reus citing Marca.

q: In 2019 a group announced it had bought Reus via a tweet. Why did it not save them?
a: The purchase came after Reus had already failed to pay their players
note: Real State Investment announced purchase by tweet 21 Jan 2019, too late for the disciplinary case: es.wikipedia citing AS and LaLiga.

q: Burgos dissolved their original club in 1983. What happened to its reserve team?
a: It broke away as Real Burgos and reached La Liga
sub: When Real Burgos faded after 1993, Burgos CF was refounded.
note: Burgos CF dissolved May 1983, Burgos Promesas became Real Burgos and played La Liga 1990-93; Burgos CF refounded: en and es.wikipedia.

q: Dmitry Piterman, later owner of Alavés, wanted to manage Racing from the touchline. How did he dodge the ban on being in the technical area?
a: He got himself accredited as a journalist or photographer
note: Piterman accredited himself as the club website photographer: Diario de León and en.wikipedia Dmitry Piterman.

q: Bilbao Athletic and Castilla finished 1983-84 level on points at the top of the Segunda. What happened in La Liga that season?
a: Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid also finished level on points, and Athletic won it
note: Both pairs level on points in 1983-84, Castilla took the Segunda and Athletic the title: es.wikipedia Bilbao Athletic and Real Madrid Castilla. Re-tagged.

q: Elche and Hércules, rivals in the Costa Blanca derby, both come from which Spanish province?
note: Both in Alicante province: es.wikipedia Hércules.

q: Under Franco, Racing de Santander had to drop their foreign-sounding name in 1941. What were they renamed?
sub: The old name came back in 1973.
note: Real Santander SD 1941-73: en and es.wikipedia Racing. Moved to hard.

q: Atlético Madrid's reserve side went back to which historic name in 2025?
note: Atlético Madrileño name from 2025: es.wikipedia Atlético Madrileño. Moved to hard.

q: Castilla CF became Real Madrid B in 1991. Why did the old name have to go?
a: The federation banned reserve teams from using separate names
sub: The Castilla name came back in 2005.
note: RFEF 1991 rule; Real Madrid B until 2005, then Real Madrid Castilla: en and es.wikipedia.

q: Xerez moved to Chapín in 1988. Which old ground did they leave behind?
sub: Chapín was opened with a game against Real Madrid.
note: Left the Estadio Domecq for Chapín 1988, opened v Real Madrid: en and es.wikipedia Xerez CD.

q: Atlético Aviación kept their La Liga place in 1939 by winning a one-off play-off in Valencia. Who did they beat?
sub: They won 3-1 at Mestalla and went on to win the league.
note: Won 3-1 at Mestalla, 26 Nov 1939: es.wikipedia Atlético de Madrid. Osasuna were not Segunda champions: es.wikipedia says they had been last in the 1935-36 Primera (en.wikipedia disagrees). Removed the label. Sub no longer gives away the Oviedo row.

q: Deportivo reached La Liga for the first time in 1941. Which club did they beat 2-1 in the promotion play-off?
note: Beat Murcia 2-1 for first promotion, 1941: en.wikipedia Deportivo. Re-tagged.

q: Which club spoiled the opening of Cádiz's Ramón de Carranza stadium in September 1955, winning 4-0?
note: Opened 3 Sep 1955, Cádiz 0-4 Barcelona: es.wikipedia Cádiz CF.

q: Real Murcia played their first official game at the Nueva Condomina in November 2006. Who were the visitors?
sub: They went up to La Liga at the end of that season.
note: First official game 26 Nov 2006 v Valladolid; Valladolid champions 2006-07: es.wikipedia Real Murcia.

q: Why could Real Oviedo not play the 1939-40 La Liga season?
a: Their ground was wrecked in the Civil War
sub: They were allowed a year off to rebuild it.
note: Ammunition dump claim is only in en.wikipedia; es.wikipedia says trenches and machine-gun nests, then bombing, left it ruined. Rewritten to the agreed fact and moved to hard.

q: One version of the Alcoyano legend has them losing heavily when the referee blew up early. How did players and fans react?
a: They protested, because they believed they could yet come back
note: Version with the early whistle and protests: es.wikipedia CD Alcoyano.

q: Real Oviedo returned to the Segunda in 2015 after 13 years away. Which club did they beat 2-1 on aggregate in the play-off?
note: Beat Cádiz 1-1, 0-1 in 2015 after 13 years away: en and es.wikipedia Real Oviedo. Re-tagged.
